member.name: T:OpenIGI.Frontend.IShellHost
member.summary: What the shell asks of the application it runs inside: starting a mission, quitting, previewing a mission behind the menu, and persisting settings.
member.remarks: The shell is backend-free and holds no window, device or game loop, so everything that needs those goes through this seam, which the desktop composition root implements. It is the same shape as the existing menu host's StartGame/quit hooks, widened for the cinematic shell's needs.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Frontend.Saves.SaveSlotStore
member.summary: Reads and writes the port's profile-scoped save slots — a small JSON manifest beside a PNG screenshot per slot — in a directory of the port's own, never the game installation.

remarks.para: This is a new, self-contained format rather than an extension of the retail config: a JSON array of in saves.json, and a profile-qualified slot-N-*.png next to it holding the frame the save was taken on. Keeping it separate means it can grow (more per-slot detail, a thumbnail size change) without any risk to the byte-compatible config.qvm the profile system guards.
Load is defensive: a missing or corrupt manifest is an empty slot list, never a throw out of a constructor, so a hand-edited or partially-written file cannot stop the shell opening.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Frontend.Screens.ExtrasScreen
member.summary: The extras section: the credits, and the developer-facing toggles — the benchmark overlay and the reminders for photo mode and the console.
member.remarks:
The benchmark toggle binds the existing r_perflog CVar, which already measures and reports the per-pass GPU timings, so "benchmark reporting per-pass timings" is the switch for a facility the renderer provides. Photo mode and the developer console are reached with the keys the game already binds; the screen points to them rather than duplicating them.
The player cheats sit behind two switches, so they are never one click away: "Developer mode" shows the section, "Enable cheats" shows the controls and puts them in force. None of them is saved.

member.name: T:OpenIGI.Frontend.Screens.ShellScreen
member.summary: The common frame every shell page shares: a header across the top — the game switcher, the section tabs between their Q and E keys, the operative and Quit — a footer of key hints across the bottom, and the page's own content between them.

remarks.para: Navigation is by replacement, not a stack: selecting a tab resets the shell to that section, so there is only ever one page on screen. The header and footer are the page's chrome: drawn outside the page's fade, so they hold still while one page gives way to the next. Back returns to the home page.
The title doubles as the game selector, opening a list of the titles the shell knows about: the name at the top left is the statement of which game is running.
Behind it all is the level, blurred () and vignetted by ; the home page leaves it sharp, because there the level is the point.
